about: The niratl recipe (telluric parameters from solar-clean pixels, HITRAN H2O shifts, solar broadening; line coupling kept on files 4 and 5) on the other Kitt Peak files, 2026-10-18. 'trial': sampled windows (every 15th of the 1983 pair, every 10th of the 1990 files) at several pressure-width scales against the then-canonical runs. 'full_1983': the full refits of the 1983 pair at x1.06, promoted the same day, against the superseded runs. Written by scripts/score_telluric_correction.py --relative-transmission (pixels below T 0.15 excluded); file 5 is also scored against photatl, the authors' correction of the same spectrum.

ftsspec_830626_2.method: niratl ships the authors' own corrected solar spectrum (Wallace, Hinkle & Livingston 1993). Ours minus theirs mixes both corrections' errors, so instead each is scored on its own, the same way: at pixels where the model transmission is below 0.97 and the solar model is flat (above 0.995 of its continuum), the rms of the corrected spectrum about a running mean of nearby pixels with neither solar nor telluric absorption. A perfect correction leaves noise there. The first and last 50 pixels are not scored: an edge pixel is inside the neighbouring page too (pages overlap by 5 cm-1), and a fit that leaves edges out should not be judged on them. Nor are pixels below a transmission of 0.15, which the corrected products blank: dividing by a saturated core turns a percent of model error into a spike that can outweigh the rest of a window. Two bins: every telluric pixel (T < 0.97) and the deep ones (T < 0.7).
